predecessors.note: 'The killing of his heir Llywelyn in 1160' follows the death of Madog ap Maredudd, which split Powys into northern and southern portions. Cliopatria's Powys row runs to 1168 and its Powys Wenwynwyn row starts in 1169.

land.text: southern Powys, which continued as a marcher lordship (the Lordship of Powis) after 1284

successors.note: The infobox runs to 1309, when Griffith de la Pole died without heirs; this dossier ends with the principality in 1284 (the page puts Owen's surrender to Edward I in 1283 'with reserve', and Owen did not succeed in possession until 1286). No Cliopatria shape exists for the lordship.

capitals.name: Mathrafal (near Meifod)
capitals.note: 'In 1212 Gwenwynwyn's ancient royal seat at Mathrafal was destroyed.' The coordinates are approximate; the page gives no location for Mathrafal.

capitals.name: Welshpool
capitals.note: Gwenwynwyn was 'restored to his realm in 1215, making a new capital at Welshpool'; the page calls the town Pool and names Powis Castle.

rulers.name: Owain Cyfeiliog
rulers.note: The map caption runs 1160-1195; he 'abdicated in 1195'. The page gives no death date.

rulers.name: Gwenwynwyn
rulers.note: Reign given as 1195-1216; he died in England in 1216 (Llywelyn the Great page). Evicted 1208 or 1212, restored 1215.

rulers.name: Gruffudd ap Gwenwynwyn
rulers.note: 'Did not return to Wales until 1241'; died in 1286 or 1287 (the page's family list); clipped here at the principality's end in 1284.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the split of Powys is 1160 (Powys Fadog page: 'Powys split in two in 1160 following the death of Prince Madog ap Maredudd'; the Wenwynwyn page's map caption begins at 1160), but Cliopatria's row starts in 1169; the 1169 shape is used for 1160-1168.

3,122 km2 (16 cells) for 1169-1205, bbox 4.07 W to 3.07 W, 52.25 N to 52.92 N. The page gives no area. The lands it names (Cyfeiliog, Arwystli, Mawddwy, Caereinion, Ystrad Marchell, Upper Mochnant, Welshpool, Powis Castle) fit the shape, but the page has Gwenwynwyn seizing the cantref of Arwystli only in 1197, so the shape draws it 28 years early (ledger gain 1197).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1206 shape, for 1206-1207 only (annexed by Llywelyn in 1208)

keyframe_review.note: Same 3,122 km2 for 1206-1209. It holds to 1207 only: 'John summoned him to Shrewsbury in October [1208] and then arrested him and stripped him of his lands' and 'Llywelyn took the opportunity to annex southern Powys and northern Ceredigion' (1208). Cliopatria ends the row in 1209 and enlarges its Gwynedd shape by 15 of these 16 cells in 1210. The Wenwynwyn page instead puts the eviction in 1212 (Mathrafal destroyed); the two pages disagree and the Llywelyn page is followed.

New keyframe, 1215 only: Gwenwynwyn was 'restored to his realm in 1215, making a new capital at Welshpool' (John 'sent troops to help restore Gwenwynwyn', undated, on the Llywelyn page); in 1216 'he was defeated in battle with the forces of Llywelyn' and died in England that year. Cliopatria has no shape for 1210-1240.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1206 shape reused for 1241-1284: Arwystli, Cyfeiliog, Mawddwy, Caereinion, Ystrad Marchell and Upper Mochnant

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1241-1284: Gruffudd ap Gwenwynwyn 'did not return to Wales until 1241 after the death of Llywelyn' and was invested with Arwystli, Cyfeiliog, Mawddwy, Caereinion, Ystrad Marchell and Upper Mochnant; he transferred his allegiance back to Llywelyn ap Gruffudd in 1263 and returned to English protection after 1276 (page). The Cliopatria shape (which has no row after 1209) is reused. The principality ends in 1284 with the Statute of Rhuddlan.

region.text: southern Powys: Cyfeiliog and the Severn and Vyrnwy valleys

ledger.note: 1160: Powys splits and the southern half is the future Powys Wenwynwyn under Owain Cyfeiliog. 'Powys split in two in 1160 following the death of Prince Madog ap Maredudd'; the Wenwynwyn page's map caption starts at 1160 and its infobox reads '1160 - 1309'.

region.text: the cantref of Arwystli around Llanidloes

ledger.counterpart: Arwystli (previous holder not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1197: Gwenwynwyn seizes the cantref of Arwystli. 'Gwenwynwyn seized the cantref of Arwystli in 1197, when he was aligned with England.' The page does not say from whom. The gazetteer has no Arwystli, so a 20 km circle round Llanidloes stands for the cantref. Cliopatria's shape includes it from 1169.

region.text: southern Powys, annexed by Llywelyn ab Iorwerth

ledger.note: 1208: John arrests Gwenwynwyn and Llywelyn annexes southern Powys. John 'summoned him to Shrewsbury in October and then arrested him and stripped him of his lands'; 'Llywelyn took the opportunity to annex southern Powys and northern Ceredigion'. The Wenwynwyn page has the eviction in 1212 ('Mathrafal was destroyed and he was evicted from his territories'); Cliopatria has Gwynedd absorb the land in 1210.
1215: Gwenwynwyn is restored to his realm and makes Welshpool his capital. 'Restored to his realm in 1215, making a new capital at Welshpool.'

1216: Llywelyn defeats Gwenwynwyn and drives him out of southern Powys again. Llywelyn drove Gwenwynwyn out of southern Powys again in 1216 (paraphrase); Wenwynwyn page: 'In 1216 he was defeated in battle with the forces of Llywelyn'. Gwenwynwyn 'died in England later that year, leaving an underage heir'; Llywelyn's 1218 Treaty of Worcester 'confirmed him in possession of all his recent conquests'.

region.text: Arwystli, Cyfeiliog, Mawddwy, Caereinion, Ystrad Marchell and Upper Mochnant

ledger.note: 1241: Gruffudd ap Gwenwynwyn returns and is invested with southern Powys. He 'did not return to Wales until 1241 after the death of Llywelyn' and was invested with Arwystli, Cyfeiliog, Mawddwy, Caereinion, Ystrad Marchell and Upper Mochnant. The page does not name who invested him; the land had been Gwynedd's since 1216.

region.text: southern Powys, the Lordship of Powis

ledger.note: 1284: the Statute of Rhuddlan ends the Welsh principalities; southern Powys becomes a marcher lordship. After the Statute of Rhuddlan in 1284 other princely titles in Wales ceased, but the principality continued as a marcher lordship (page, partly paraphrased); Owain 'allegedly surrendered the principality of Powys to Edward I at the Parliament held in Shrewsbury in 1283' (to be 'accepted with reserve'); Owen did not succeed in possession until 1286.

1284: the princely state of Powys Wenwynwyn ends; the land continues as the Lordship of Powis to 1309. The infobox reads '1160 - 1309'; 'When Griffith de la Pole died without heirs in 1309' the lordship passed to his sister Hawise.

wars.name: Llywelyn the Great's annexation of southern Powys
wars.outcome: John arrested Gwenwynwyn in October 1208 and Llywelyn annexed southern Powys; Mathrafal was destroyed in 1212; Gwenwynwyn was restored in 1215 and defeated by Llywelyn in 1216, dying in England that year; the 1218 Treaty of Worcester confirmed Llywelyn's conquests.
wars.note: The Wenwynwyn page puts the eviction in 1212 and the restoration in 1215; the Llywelyn page puts John's help for the restoration without a year.

wars.name: Edward I's conquest of Wales
wars.outcome: Gruffudd ap Gwenwynwyn returned to English protection 'after 1276' following a failed plot against Llywelyn; his soldiers helped kill Llywelyn ap Gruffudd near Builth in 1282 and mobilised in the Welsh War of 1282-1283; the principality ended in 1283-1284.

certainty.note: The cantref boundaries are approximate and no treaty line is on the pages; the Welsh-English frontier on the Severn and Vyrnwy (Shropshire) is unsurveyed.

notes: Pages: 3 of 1-2 budgeted (Powys Wenwynwyn, Llywelyn the Great and the Powys Fadog page shared for the 1160 split); the Fadog page was opened for the other dossier. Cliopatria's row is 1169-1209 in two identical shapes (1169-1205, 1206-1209); the page gives 1160-1309 (infobox). This dossier starts in 1160 (the Powys dossier ends then), ends in 1284 with the principality (Statute of Rhuddlan), and adds keyframes for 1160-1168, 1215 and 1241-1284 that reuse Cliopatria's shape. Years 1208-1214 and 1216-1240 have no land: the land is Llywelyn's (Cliopatria's Gwynedd shape takes 15 of the 16 cells in 1210; the Gwynedd dossier has gain 1208 from this state). DISAGREEMENT: the Llywelyn page has Gwenwynwyn stripped of his lands in October 1208 and southern Powys annexed that year; the Wenwynwyn page has him evicted in 1212; the 1208 date is followed (it names the land and is nearer Cliopatria's 1209/1210). END: infobox 1309 and a lordship that continues; the state ends with the princely title in 1284; no Cliopatria shape exists for the Lordship of Powis, so the lordship 1285-1309 is not drawn here. Vassalage: Gruffudd 'transferred his allegiance back to Llywelyn ap Gruffudd in 1263' and returned to English protection 'after 1276' (both on the Wenwynwyn page); the Gwynedd dossier already records vassal_start 1263 and vassal_end 1274 for this state, so no vassal event is repeated here. Area: no figure on the page. Gazetteer names needed: Cyfeiliog, Arwystli, Mawddwy, Caereinion, Ystrad Marchell, Mochnant, Powis; Mathrafal coordinates are approximate. Failed pages: none.
